gap: No result ChatGPT got states which 5,000 W-plus single units the makers' own US stores list as buyable now and at what price: on 2026-11-27 that was the Nature's Generator L6000 at $2,249.99 and the OUPES Guardian 6000 V2 at $2,699, neither of which ChatGPT named, while two of its three picks (EcoFlow DELTA Pro Ultra, Anker F3800 Plus) are sold out at their makers and the Pecron F5000LFP and EcoFlow TITAN 5000 Plus are pre-orders shipping in January.
standout_why: I opened four of the results: solarwaypoint.com (cited), holdbackup.com (cited), powerbencher.com and thewattguide.com. None prints a price. holdbackup gives stock status dated Nov 2, 2026 for five units (F3800 Plus sold out, Jackery sold out/pre-order, DELTA Pro Ultra limited stock), so it has part of the stock picture, 25 days old. thewattguide lists the Pecron as a pre-order (October) and the OUPES Guardian 6000 V2, with no prices. None of the four lists the Nature's Generator L6000. Not opened, so not compared: outboundpower.com (HTTP 429), runtimewise, thiswatt, enoughwatts, wattsift, theoutageplan, homepowerfacts, powersized, power-specs, popularmechanics. Every price and stock figure below except Anker's comes from the store's own search listing; all product-page reads returned HTTP 429, so variant-level price and stock are not confirmed.
decides: It moves the pick off ChatGPT's Jackery for a shopper who wants a unit now at the lowest price read: the L6000 (ours) is listed in stock at $2,249.99, $1,249.01 under Jackery's $3,499 listing, with 6,000 W at 120/240 V. It loses on battery size: 3,840 Wh is about 46 minutes at 5,000 W before losses, against about 60 for the Jackery. The OUPES Guardian 6000 V2 is the honest near-tie: same dollars per Wh, 768 Wh more, $449.01 more, also listed in stock. The Jackery stays the pick for 7,200 W and 5,040 Wh if its single unit is in stock, which I could not confirm. The Pecron is the lowest per Wh but ships early January, so by the four-week rule it cannot be the pick. The L6000 sale end date (Nov 29 in the desk notes) was not confirmed today.
candidates: BLUETTI RV5 + B4810 (5,000 W RV system, not a portable unit)
Anker SOLIX S5000 (4,500 W, just short)
EcoFlow TITAN 5000 Classic (4,000 W, just short)
